               Primary Efficacy Analysis
               The primary efficacy analysis was performed on the clinically evaluable and the ITT co-primary
               analysis sets. The primary efficacy endpoint was the clinical cure rate at the TOC visit, defined
               as the ratio of the number of subjects who had a derived clinical outcome of cure at the TOC
               visit to the total number of the subjects in the analysis set under consideration.
               The hypotheses tested were:
                   H0: The clinical cure rate of the ceftobiprole arm is more than 10% inferior to that of the
                         ceftriaxone with or without linezolid arm.
                   H1: The clinical cure rate of the ceftobiprole arm is no more than 10% inferior to that of the
                         ceftriaxone with or without linezolid arm.
               A 2-sided 95% confidence interval based on the Normal approximation for the difference of two
               binomial proportions was calculated for the between-treatment difference (ceftobiprole minus
               ceftriaxone with or without linezolid) at the TOC Visit. Noninferiority of ceftobiprole compared
               with ceftriaxone with or without linezolid was concluded if the lower limit of this confidence
               interval was greater than or equal to –10%.

               Secondary Efficacy Analyses
               The secondary efficacy endpoints were tested using a step-down hierarchical procedure in the
               following order:
                    1) microbiological eradication rate at the TOC visit,
                    2) clinical cure rate at the TOC visit for subjects who had a PSI score ≥91,
                    3) the 30-day pneumonia-specific mortality rates.
               The microbiological eradication rate at the TOC Visit was defined as the ratio of the number of
               subjects with a microbiological outcome of Eradication or Presumed Eradication at the TOC visit
               to the total number of subjects in the analysis set under consideration at the TOC visit. This
               analysis was performed on the microbiologically evaluable analysis set.
               The clinical cure rate for subjects who had a PSI score ≥91 was defined as the ratio of the
               number of subjects with PSI score ≥91 who had a clinical outcome of cure at the TOC visit to the
               total number of the subjects with a PSI score ≥91 in the analysis set under consideration. The
               analysis of the clinical cure rate for subjects who had a PSI score ≥91 was performed on the
               clinically evaluable and ITT analysis sets.
               Noninferiority hypotheses similar to the primary hypothesis were tested for the microbiological
               eradication rate and the clinical response rate in subjects with a PSI score ≥91.

               The protocol specified two co-primary endpoints to be analyzed in the primary efficacy analysis,

               (95% CI: -9.3, 3.6) which indicated NI since the lower bound of -9.3% exceeded the -10% limit.

                    6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues

                        6.3.1. Re-Analysis of Trial CAP-3001
               Issue
               CAP-3001 was conducted prior to the CABP Guidance of 2020 and was not designed to assess
               an early clinical success endpoint (Day 4) in an appropriate Trial population (e.g., PORT Risk
               Class ≥ III) in which a non-inferiority margin could be scientifically justified. Therefore, the
               Applicant provided several post-hoc re-analyses which considered new analysis populations,
               endpoints, and selection criteria which closely followed those outlined in the CABP Guidance4.
               Background
               Since Trial CAP-3001 was conducted from June 2006 to July 2007, i.e., before the current FDA
               CABP Guidance for Industry was issued in June 2020, the Applicant included CSR Addendum 2
               in this NDA submission. Addendum 2 included additional post-hoc analyses that were performed
               after completion of the original CSR (dated November 3, 2009). These new analyses shown in
               the tables below were taken directly from Addendum 2 of the CSR. These analyses were critical
               in assessing the overall evidence obtained from this Trial and the Trial’s ability to meet the
               current recommendations for CABP trials outlined in the FDA Guidance.
               The endpoints and Trial populations specified in the re-analysis were similar to those described
               in the Guidance. The primary endpoint in Trial CAP-3001 was clinical cure at the TOC visit
               which clearly differed from the endpoint of clinical success at Day 4 stipulated in the current
               guidance. Therefore, the re-analyses considered an early clinical response endpoint at Day 3
               (prior to IV to oral switch) which resembled the Guidance endpoint at Day 4, as shown in Table
               39. There were also differences in the Trial populations of CAP-3001 and the Guidance. The
               Applicant modified the analysis populations to be more consistent with the FDA Guidance.
               There were also differences between the original entry criteria of CAP-3001 and those outlined
               in the Guidance are shown in Table 40.

               Analysis Populations for the Re-analysis
               In total, four analysis populations were used for the re-analyses using the primary endpoint
               stipulated in the 2020 FDA CABP guidance:
               •    The ‘Day 3-ITT population’ comprised all randomized subjects who had at least two of the
                    following symptoms at baseline: tachypnea, cough, production of purulent sputum, or chest
                    pain. Subjects were analyzed according to the study medication assigned at randomization.
               •    The Day 3-modified ITT population comprised the subset of subjects in the Day 3-ITT
                    population who met all of the following additional criteria: 1. At least one of new-onset
                    hypoxemia, rales or pulmonary consolidation, and leukocytosis or leukopenia. 2. At least two
                    of fever, hypothermia, hypotension, tachycardia, and tachypnea.
               •    The Day 3-mITT population was the subset of the Day 3-ITT subjects who had a valid
                    pathogen at baseline.
               •    The Day 3-modified mITT population was the subset of the Day 3-modified ITT subjects
                    who had a valid pathogen at baseline.
               The Baseline demographic and disease characteristics in the ‘Day 3-ITT population’ and the
               ‘Day 3-modified ITT population’ are shown in Table 39.

               Primary Efficacy Analysis in Re-analysis
               The re-analysis was performed to determine whether ceftobiprole is non-inferior to ceftriaxone ±
               linezolid for the primary endpoint of clinical success at Day 3. Analysis of the primary endpoint
               was based on the Day 3-ITT population and the Day 3-modified ITT population.
               A two-sided 95% confidence interval using the Normal approximation to the difference of two
               binomial proportions, was calculated for the between-treatment difference (ceftobiprole minus
               ceftriaxone ± linezolid) at the TOC Visit.
               The result for the primary endpoint of the re-analysis was interpreted in the context of a 12.5%
               non-inferiority margin, i.e., non-inferiority of ceftobiprole compared with ceftriaxone with or
               without linezolid was interpreted if the lower limit of this confidence interval was greater than or
               equal to −12.5%.
               The same subgroup analyses were performed for the re-analysis of the primary endpoint in
               accordance with the 2020 FDA CABP guidance as described for the pre-specified primary
               endpoint of derived clinical cure at the TOC Visit (CAP-3001 CSR Appendix 2.2.1.1). The
               exception is the subgroup analysis by oral switch status, as none of the subjects in the Trial had
               switched to oral therapy at the Day 3 assessment.

               Reviewer Comments
               The 12.5% NI margin mentioned above was chosen by the Applicant to be wider than the 10% NI
               margin for the original primary analysis to account for additional variability from having to
               reduce the size of the analysis populations to be consistent with the guidelines for populations
               specified in the 2020 CABP Guidance. However, since a NI margin of 10% was satisfied in the
               re-analyses for early clinical success in the Day 3 ITT and Day 3 mITT populations (as
               discussed later in this section), this change in the margin did not impact conclusions.

                        6.3.2. Clinical Success in Ukrainian Versus Non-
                              Ukrainian Sites in Trial BPR-CS-009
               Issue
               In Trial BPR-CS-009, it was observed that sites in Ukraine showed substantially higher overall
               success rates compared to sites in other countries. Due to large site-specific efficacy and fewer
               AEs, these sites were identified for inspection but could not be inspected due to the current travel
               restrictions to Ukraine. Thus, in addition to clinical site inspections, an Applicant inspection was
               also conducted (see Section 10 for details), and higher overall success in Ukraine was evaluated
               in further detail.

               Background
               There may be limitations with generalizing Trial findings across different geographical regions.
               Overall response rates in non-Ukrainian countries may be lower than rates observed in the
               Trial BPR-CS-009, which included Ukrainian sites with high response rates. Ukraine was
               also the highest-enrolling country in the Trial, with 46.5% of subjects (180/387) in
               the mITT population. This may also have implications for the assumptions used in justifying the
               non-inferiority margin since the subject populations of Ukraine may not be appropriate for
               inclusion due to inherently lower risk factors and more effective therapeutic interventions
               compared to those of the assumed study population.
               Based on post-hoc analyses, subjects enrolled in Ukraine were younger and had a more favorable
               distribution of Baseline categories for complicated SAB, e.g., the percentage of subjects on
               chronic dialysis was 0.6% (1/180) in Ukraine compared to 23.2% (48/207) in other countries,
               and there were no subjects with LIE from Ukraine vs 4.8% (10/207) in other countries.
               Therapeutic interventions with the potential for achieving source control for SAB were
               performed more often within 72 hours before, or within 7 days after, randomization, in subjects
               from Ukraine than in other countries, e.g., in 70.5% for abdominal abscesses in Ukraine
               compared to 9.1% in abdominal abscesses in other countries, and in 67.9% (74/109) in
               ABSSSIs/soft tissue infections in Ukraine compared to 30.5% (30/128) in other countries. (Table
               45).

               Significantly higher overall success rates based on DRC at the PTE visit were observed in

               As noted above, concerns were lessened since the between-arm difference was not more
               favorable in Ukraine versus the other countries. However, real life comparisons of rates may be
               lower than what was observed in this Trial due to the high rates observed in Ukraine, therefore
               comparisons of rates in the potential labeling should describe the strong differences in overall

               7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)

                    7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on
                        Nonclinical Data
               The nonclinical safety profile of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium has been explored in single and
               repeat-dose studies in mice, rats, dogs, rabbits and monkeys for up to 3 months duration; in vitro
               and in vivo genotoxicity studies; reproductive and developmental toxicity studies including
               fertility studies in male and female rats, embryofetal developmental studies in rats and monkeys,
               and pre- and post-natal developmental toxicity study in rats; and PK and toxicokinetic studies to
               support ceftobiprole medocaril sodium development and to compare PK in animals and humans.
               The target organs of toxicity that may be relevant to human risks are described below.

               Injection Site Reactions, Thrombi, Emboli, Convulsions, Mortality
               Thrombi formation at the injection site was a consistent finding in toxicological studies across
               species, including rats, marmosets and dogs with severity increasing with dosing duration. In 2-
               4- and 13-week studies in rats, marmosets, and dogs, injection site findings included thrombus
               formation, accumulation of inflammatory cells, thickening of the vascular wall in the periphery
               of the dosing catheter, granulomas, edema/hemorrhage and/or necrosis of tissues around the
               catheter. No other significant toxicities were observed in 2-week studies in rats and in 4-week
               studies in rats and marmosets administered ceftobiprole medocaril sodium (at doses up to
               360 mg/kg/day (1.4-times the maximum recommended human dose [MRHD] based on body
               surface area [BSA] comparisons) and 200 mg/kg/day respectively, (0.75 times the MRHD, based
               on BSA comparisons). However, in the 13-week studies in the rats and marmosets at similar
               doses to those used in shorter term studies, convulsions and mortality were observed (≥50 mg/kg
               in marmosets, 0.2 times the MRHD; ≥250 mg/kg in rats, 0.94 times the MRHD, based on BSA
               comparisons). Thrombi/emboli were seen in marmosets in several tissues distal to the site of
               injection, including in skeletal muscle, heart, and lungs, that were attributed to the cause of
               mortality at all doses tested. In the rat 13-week study, mortality was primarily attributed to
               kidney failure (see kidney toxicity information below). Although no seizures or thrombi (except
               at the injection site) were reported in the dog 13-week study (up to 32 mg/kg/day, 0.4 timed the
               MRHD, based on BSA comparisons), the dosing catheter in many animals did not remain patent
               for the duration of the study and was found to be filled with fibrin, erythrocyte clumps and
               inflammatory cell infiltrate. In mice, tonic/clonic convulsions were observed after ceftobiprole
               medocaril sodium was administered as a single intravenous dose at ≥250 mg/kg (0.75 times the
               MRHD, based on BSA comparisons).

               Kidney Toxicity
               No significant kidney toxicities were observed in 2- or 4-week studies in rats or in 4-week
               studies in marmosets. However, in a 13-week rat study at doses up to 750 mg/kg/day in males
               (2.8 times the MRHD, based on BSA comparisons) and 376 mg/kg/day in females (1.42 time the
               MRHD, based on BSA comparisons), significant kidney toxicity (dose dependent increases in
               tubular/duct eosinophilic bodies, and presence of foreign material) was observed at
               ≥250 mg/kg/day potentially due to precipitation of test article; kidney interstitial fibrosis
               (moderate) was observed in males at the high dose. Mortality was observed at ≥250 mg/kg/day,

               MRHD based on BSA comparisons), showed moderate antigenic potential.


                    7.2. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on
                        Drug Class or Other Drug-Specific Factors
               Ceftobiprole is a cephalosporin antibacterial drug. In general, cephalosporins have a favorable
               safety profile and have been well-tolerated with extensive use worldwide. Common adverse
               reactions associated with their use include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rash.
               Labeled Warnings and Precautions across the five generations of cephalosporins include serious
               hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions, Clostridioides difficile associated diarrhea, neurotoxicity
               including seizures and encephalopathy, development of drug-resistant bacteria with prolonged or
               inappropriate use, and laboratory-based abnormalities such as direct Coombs’ test
               seroconversion and decrease in prothrombin activity. Almost all cephalosporins require dose
               adjustment in subjects with impaired renal function. The second generation cephalosporins carry
               a risk of hearing loss in pediatric subjects while third generation cephalosporins such as
               ceftriaxone may interact with calcium containing products, or cause pancreatitis, biliary sludge,
               gallbladder pseudolithiasis, and hemolytic anemia. Third and fourth generation cephalosporins
               have rarely been associated with electrolyte derangements including hyponatremia and
               hyperkalemia.
               Reported post-marketing adverse events for cephalosporins include serum sickness-like reaction,
               acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis. A few cases of
               neonatal death in subjects receiving ceftriaxone in conjunction with calcium-containing fluids
               have been reported. Hepatotoxicity or drug induced liver injury due to cephalosporins are
               uncommon with the exception of ceftriaxone which as noted above can cause biliary sludge
               related to the formation of ceftriaxone-calcium salt. Finally, there have been reports of life-
               threatening or fatal occurrences of encephalopathy, myoclonus and seizures related to cefepime
               use. This was primarily observed in subjects with renal impairment who exceeded recommended
               dosages but have also occurred in subjects in whom doses were appropriately adjusted.

                    7.3. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Identified
                        Through Postmarket Experience
               A review of the literature regarding the postmarketing experience for ceftobiprole yielded a
               retrospective case series conducted in Italy reporting on 29 patients who received ceftobiprole; 2
               patients developed myoclonus and 1 patient developed a rash that were attributed to ceftobiprole
               (Durante-Mangoni et al. 2020). No deaths occurred in patients while receiving ceftobiprole.
               Another published case reported agranulocytosis in a patient receiving ceftobiprole after DRESS
               associated with vancomycin and rifampin (Wendland et al. 2011). After discontinuation of
               ceftobiprole, the patient’s neutrophils recovered without further issues. The Applicant has also
               submitted postmarketing surveillance data in their application highlighting cases of serious
               hypersensitivity reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, urticaria, and angioedema.
               The FDA Adverse Event Reporting System was also queried for AEs reported with ceftobiprole.
               Upon review, AEs that were deemed potentially related to ceftobiprole were leukopenia,
               encephalopathy, rash, agranulocytosis, hyponatremia, and seizures.
               Review of the labeling from Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia did not identify any
               new safety issues. Safety issues and adverse reactions reported in the ex-US labeling were
               derived from the clinical studies covered in this review. No additional postmarketing experiences
               were identified.


                    7.4. FDA Approach to the Safety Review
               Please see the discussion in Section 3.2 for a description of the clinical trials and any other data
               used in the review of safety and whether the trials submitted were fit for purpose. The studies
               submitted for safety were analyzed individually as described in this section. Pooling of safety
               results was not deemed to be appropriate given clinically distinct subject populations and
               differences in study design and conduct across pivotal trials. No major data quality or integrity
               issues were identified that would preclude performing a safety review for this NDA. There were
               no major identified issues with respect to recording, coding and categorizing AEs. A few
               preferred terms (PTs) were reclassified based on the verbatim terms. The clinical data scientist
               performed standard safety analyses including Food and Drug Administration Medical Dictionary
               for Regulatory Activities queries (FMQs) to determine safety signals, and additional analyses as
               requested by the clinical team. The clinical review team performed a grouped query (GQ)
               analysis for selected treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) to evaluate potential splitting
               of similar AEs and these are discussed in the TEAE section of each indication. Review of subject
               narratives and graphical subject profiles (created using JMP clinical version 17) were used in
               some instances to help determine causality. AE and TEAE are used interchangeably in this
               review.

                           7.6.1.2. Deaths, Trial BPR-CS-009
               There were no imbalances in TEAEs leading to death between the treatment arms (17/191
               (8.9%) in the ceftobiprole and 18/198 (9.1%) in the daptomycin arm). In both arms, the most
               commonly reported TEAE leading to death was multiple organ dysfunction syndrome and septic
               shock.
               None of the TEAEs leading to death were assessed as drug related by the investigator or by the
               FDA reviewer upon a detailed review of the case narratives. The case narratives and subject
               profiles suggested that the deaths appeared to be related to underlying comorbidities and
               complications arising from the underlying infection, which is not unexpected for subjects with
               SAB. A meta-analysis performed in 2022 estimated that the all-cause mortality rate of SAB in a
               total of 341 studies (536,791 subjects, spanning from January 1, 1991 to May 7, 2021) was
               10.4% (95% CI, 9.0%–12.1%) at 7 days, 13.3% (95% CI, 11.1%–15.8%) at 2 weeks, 18.1%
               (95% CI, 16.3%–20.0%) at 1 month, 27.0% (95% CI, 21.5%–33.3%) at 3 months, and 30.2%
               (95% CI, 22.4%–39.3%) at 1 year (Bai et al. 2022).
               The mortality rate in the BPR-CS-009 trial of 8.9% at Day 70 was less than what was seen in the
               meta-analysis by Bai et al. described above, possibly due to mortality being assessed in a clinical
               trial setting.

                    As described below, two subjects in the ceftobiprole arm, who had no past medical history of
                    seizures, developed SAEs of seizures that were temporally associated with ceftobiprole.
                    Cephalosporins can precipitate seizures and seizures are noted as warnings in the labeling of
                    several drugs in this class (Bora et al. 2016). The FDA reviewer agrees with the inclusion of
                    seizures and other central nervous system disorders in the warnings section of labeling as
                    proposed by the Applicant.
               •
                                        (b) (6)
                    Subject                     had no medical history of seizure and developed an SAE of a
                    generalized tonic-clonic seizure on Day 15 while on ceftobiprole, in the setting of worsening
                    renal function, and other TEAEs including nausea, vomiting, hypotension, multiple organ
                    failure with respiratory distress requiring endotracheal intubation. While there may have been
                    confounding factors such as hypotension and possible hypoxia due to respiratory distress
                    requiring intubation, an association to ceftobiprole cannot be completely excluded.
               •
                                        (b) (6)
                    Subject                     had a medical history of alcohol abuse but no history of seizures and
                    developed an SAE of seizure on Day 11 during infusion of ceftobiprole which led
                    discontinuation. At the time of the seizure, the subject was still conscious but was
                    unresponsive to a verbal challenge with a fixed glare. There were no concomitant
                    medications or events at the time that would predispose to seizures, and there was no renal
                    impairment. The FDA reviewer agrees with the investigator that this SAE was probably
                    related to ceftobiprole.

               •
                                      (b) (6)
                    Subject                   had an SAE of acute kidney injury on Day 24, two days after
                    completion of treatment with ceftobiprole. The baseline creatinine was 1.02 mg/dL (Day -1)
                    and increased to 1.3 mg/dL on Day 14 and 2.92 mg/dL on Day 21. On Day 34, a biopsy of
                    the kidney was performed which showed acute glomerulonephritis with IgA deposits

                    direct relationship between acute kidney injury and ceftobiprole. On Day 66, the subject died
                    due to respiratory failure.

                    that the renal impairment was primarily caused by ceftobiprole as the creatinine decreased

                           7.6.1.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-CS-
                                   009
               TEAEs occurred in 63.4% of the subjects in the ceftobiprole arm and 59.1% in the daptomycin
               arm with a risk difference of 4.3%. The GQs demonstrating a risk difference of at least 4% or
               higher in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the daptomycin arm were nausea, vomiting,
               hypokalemia, pneumonia, and diarrhea; these are described below. Hypokalemia is discussed in
               the laboratory Section 7.6.1.6. Although the GQ of bacterial infections were common in both
               arms, it was not considered an adverse reaction as they were likely related to underlying medical
               conditions and was not caused by ceftobiprole.

               Gastrointestinal Symptoms
               Most TEAEs of either nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea were of mild to moderate severity and did
               not lead to discontinuation. About half of the TEAEs of nausea or vomiting were related to
               ceftobiprole by the investigator.
               There were no reports of diarrhea associated with Clostridioides difficile. Gastrointestinal
               symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are often considered common adverse
               reactions associated with antibacterial drugs, and are proposed by the Applicant in Section 6 of
               labeling.

               Pneumonia
               The narrow FMQ of pneumonia encompassed the PTs of pneumonia, pneumonia staphylococcal,
               pneumonia aspiration, lung abscess, pneumonia pseudomonal, pneumonia viral, and infectious
               pleural effusion. Although the number of subjects with pneumonia was higher in the ceftobiprole
               arm compared to the daptomycin arm [16 (8.4%) versus 5 (2.5%)], review of subject profiles and
               narratives did not reveal a link between ceftobiprole and the PTs in the narrow FMQ. Out of the
               16 subjects with FMQs of pneumonia, 2 were due to aspiration and 1 was due to a viral cause. In
               most of the cases the subjects had comorbidities which made pneumonia more likely to occur
               (presence of endotracheal tube, immunosuppression, prolonged hospitalization). There was also
               no information about the pathogen except in 4 cases, where all but one of the pathogens isolated
               was gram negative. The subject with a S. aureus pneumonia is described below:

                    from lavage from the endotracheal tube; ceftobiprole was discontinued and changed to
                    imipenem-cilastatin. The AEs of pneumonia staphylococcal and respiratory failure were

                             7.6.1.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial BPR-CS-009

               Chemistry
               Chemistry findings between the two arms were similar with exception of decreased potassium,
               elevated chloride, elevated random glucose, elevated albumin and elevated blood urea nitrogen
               (BUN) which had more than a 2% risk difference of occurring in the ceftobiprole arm than in the
               daptomycin arm. None of the differences in the chemistry findings, with exception to
               hypokalemia, were felt to be directly due to ceftobiprole given that chemistry derangements are

               common in critically ill subjects. There were no laboratory measurements for lipase, amylase,
               phosphate, magnesium, calcium, and bicarbonate.

               Hypokalemia
               There was a greater frequency of AEs of blood potassium increased (GQ of hypokalemia) in the
               ceftobiprole arm as compared with the daptomycin arm, as shown in Table 52 above; this
               correlated with an increased number of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with low potassium
               values as noted in the table below. Hypokalemia could be explained by increased gastrointestinal
               losses caused by diarrhea and vomiting; both of which were higher in the ceftobiprole arm. As
               such, hypokalemia will be added to the Applicant’s proposed labeling as an adverse reaction.
               Moreover, in the ceftobiprole arm, there were 14 subjects with a low potassium value of level 3.
               In contrast, 9 subjects in the daptomycin arm had the same level with a risk difference of 2.8%,
               higher in the ceftobiprole arm. Subject profiles were evaluated for cardiac events that could be
               associated with hypokalemia. Upon examination of the 14 subjects, two subjects had AEs related
               to cardiac arrythmias, atrial fibrillation and arrhythmia, described below:
               •
                                     (b) (6)
                    Subject                reported an AE of arrhythmia on Day 12. The subject had a medical
                    history of hypertension, myocardial ischemia, myocardial infarction, diabetes mellitus, renal
                    failure, cardiac ventricular thrombosis, decubitus ulcer, intermittent hypokalemia,
                    intermittent hypernatremia, and atrial fibrillation. The nadir for potassium measurement
                    occurred on Day 3 where it was measured at 2.3 mmol/L and the subject was given
                    potassium chloride. On Day 12, the subject experienced an SAE of arrhythmia and despite
                    cardiopulmonary resuscitation and adrenaline, the subject died. No potassium level was
                    recorded on this day with the last potassium level of 3.2 mmol/L being recorded on Day 7.

                    standing order of electrolyte replacement (calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, potassium

                           7.6.1.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-009
               Several subgroups were examined based on demographic variables. For most subgroups, the
               percent of AEs occurred at similar rates. However, there was a higher percentage of AEs in
               subjects ≥65 years old in the ceftobiprole arm as compared to the daptomycin arm. There was
               also a higher percentage of AEs seen in subjects ≥65 years old compared to subjects ≤65 years
               old within the group of subjects receiving ceftobiprole, however, the types of AEs seen were
               similar. A similar trend was seen among subjects ≥75 years old, however, the size of this
               subgroup was small. In the subgroup of subjects ≥75 years old, there was a similar frequency of
               SAEs (seven subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (41%) experienced 13 SAEs while 10 subjects in
               the daptomycin arm (48%) experienced 19 SAEs). In terms of mortality, there were 6 deaths in
               the ceftobiprole arm (35%) compared to 7 deaths in the daptomycin arm (33%). The FDA
               reviewer agrees with the investigator that none of these SAEs or deaths in the ceftobiprole arm
               could be attributed to the drug.
               In addition, the majority of subjects were White, non-Hispanic or Latino, and from outside of the
               US. The frequency of AEs in these subgroups was similar to the frequency of AEs occurring in
               the entire safety population. The other demographic groups were too small to make any
               conclusions regarding safety, but no major differences are anticipated.

                           7.6.2.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BPR-CS-
                                   008
               AEs occurred in 148 of 334 subjects (44.3%) in the ceftobiprole arm and in 131 of 342 subjects
               (38.3%) in the comparator arm. The AEs that occurred with a risk difference of ≥1% in the
               ceftobiprole arm were gastrointestinal-related such as nausea (10.8% vs 5.6%), diarrhea (6.3% vs
               4.7%), and dysgeusia (2.1% vs 0%). All AEs of nausea, vomiting or diarrhea were of mild to
               moderate severity and the majority had dose interruption or modification. More than half of these
               AEs were thought to be possibly/probably related to ceftobiprole by the investigator. As with the
               009 trial, the GQ of bacterial infection was common in both arm but was not related to
               ceftobiprole and likely related to underlying medical conditions and was therefore, not included
               in the label.
               There were no reports of diarrhea associated with Clostridioides difficile. Gastrointestinal
               symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are often considered common adverse
               reactions associated with antibacterial drugs, and are proposed by the Applicant in labeling.

               The AEs related to leukopenia were reported in three subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (0.9%) and
               2 subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm (0.6%). The TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm

                        7.6.2.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial BPR-CS-008
               Table 72 shows the incidence of common TEAEs by demographic subgroups of sex, age,
               ethnicity, and race. The incidence of TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm was higher in subjects
               between the age of 18 to 34 years and the most common TEAEs are discussed below. There were
               more TEAES in the subgroup of subjects ages 65-75 years in the ceftobiprole arm as compared
               to the vancomycin and aztreonam arm, but the number of subjects was too small to draw any
               meaningful conclusions. The majority of subjects were White, non-Hispanic or Latino, and from
               the US; the incidence of TEAEs appeared to be overall similar to the safety population. In
               addition, there did not appear to be imbalances in TEAEs by gender.

               Age 18 to 34 years
               In this age group, there was a higher percentage of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm (58.6%) who
               experienced AEs compared to the percentage of subjects in the vancomycin and aztreonam arm
               (40.3%). In addition, the percentage of TEAEs in the younger subgroup was higher than in the
               older subgroups receiving ceftobiprole. The most commonly reported AEs in the ceftobiprole
               arm were nausea (n = 14), headache (n = 5), diarrhea (n = 5), alanine aminotransferase increased
               (5 subjects), and aspartate aminotransferase increased (5 subjects). The most commonly reported
               AEs in the comparator arm were headache (6 subjects), diarrhea (5 subjects), nausea (4 subjects),
               abscess limb (4 subjects), and pyrexia (3). It appears that nausea and increased liver tests may
               have driven this difference between treatment arms in this subgroup of younger subjects. In this

                            7.6.3.4. Adverse Events Leading to Treatment
                                    Discontinuation, Trial CAP-3001
               The overall rate of AEs leading to discontinuation was low at less than 10% in each trial arm
               (Table 76). The ceftobiprole arm had a higher rate of AEs leading to discontinuation compared to
               ceftriaxone at 5.8% vs 3.7%. The higher rate of AEs leading to discontinuation in the
               ceftobiprole arm was mainly due to gastrointestinal disorders with subjects experiencing
               vomiting, abdominal pain, and nausea compared to 1 subject experiencing abdominal distension
               leading to discontinuation in the ceftriaxone arm. Similar to SAEs, infections and infestations
               disorders were also relatively common in both arms. These results suggest ceftobiprole is
               relatively well tolerated with the drug leading to discontinuation in a relatively small percentage
               of subjects. Of note, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain will be labeled as adverse reactions in
               Section 6 of labeling.

                            7.6.3.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial CAP-3001
               There were slightly more TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm (70%) compared to the ceftriaxone arm
               (64.6%; Table 77). However, there is a notable difference between the types of TEAEs in each
               treatment arm. The TEAEs that occurred at a greater frequency in the ceftobiprole arm compared
               to the ceftriaxone arm included nausea, vomiting, rash, phlebitis, and hemorrhage (≥2% risk
               difference). Gastrointestinal related AEs were the most common AEs associated with the use of
               ceftobiprole. In addition, there are TEAEs in both arms that were balanced (liver enzyme

               drugs being cephalosporins or due to underlying medical comorbidities. Pneumonia was also
               balanced in both arms occurring at a high frequency however this is likely due to the underlying
               illness of the subject. Please refer to Section 17.4 for the table of subjects with all AEs occurring
               in the safety population.
               Given the higher frequency of hemorrhage in the ceftobiprole arm, these subjects were evaluated
               in greater detail. There were 4 cases of hemoptysis categorized under hemorrhage. Two of the
               subjects may have developed hemoptysis that did not have an obvious cause aside from their
               underlying pulmonary illness. Of the remaining two, one subject was on warfarin and aspirin and
               the other developed hemoptysis 12 days after receiving the last dose of ceftobiprole and was also
               diagnosed with lung cancer. For the other subjects who developed hemorrhage as an AE, three of
               the subjects were on anti-coagulant medications and 4 subjects developed their AE several days
               to weeks after receiving their last dose of ceftobiprole. There were two subjects that developed
               hematoma and ecchymoses without a clear inciting event, however one of the subjects had only
               received one day of treatment. Based on these evaluations, there does not appear to be a strong
               signal that would indicate ceftobiprole is associated with hemorrhage as several of the AEs were
               likely due to concomitant use of anti-coagulant medications or occurred after treatment.

                        7.6.3.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial CAP-3001
               The number of subjects with either high or low chemistry analyte values were generally balanced
               between the two treatment arms (Table 78). There were slightly more abnormalities in the
               ceftriaxone arm with low sodium and elevated BUN. Elevated creatinine was also seen more
               frequently in the ceftriaxone arm at 4.1% compared to 1.1% in the ceftobiprole arm (Table 79).
               There were more cases of high potassium (6.5% vs 3.6%) and low glucose (5.5% vs 3%) in the
               ceftobiprole subjects. Of note, hyperkalemia and hypoglycemia were reported as AEs less
               commonly for ceftobiprole compared to ceftriaxone. The number of subjects with liver
               abnormalities were balanced with no major differences between the two arms (Table 80). Total
               cholesterol and triglycerides were also balanced between the two arms (Table 81). Regarding
               hematology laboratory values, leukocytosis was observed more in the ceftriaxone arm at 31%
               compared with 24% in the ceftobiprole arm (Table 82). The remainder of abnormal hematologic
               values were otherwise balanced.
               Overall, there does not appear to be any major difference between ceftobiprole and ceftriaxone
               with respect to chemical, renal, cholesterol, hepatic, or hematologic laboratory values.

               Review of the vital signs data showed no clinical differences between the treatment arms. Over

               blood pressure.

                           7.6.3.9. Subgroup Analyses, Trial CAP-3001
               Based on the sub-group analysis (Table 84), there were more subjects with reported AEs in the
               ceftobiprole arm reported in each sex, race, ethnicity, and geographic subgroup which is
               consistent with the higher rate of AEs in the general population. Of note, there were fewer
               ceftobiprole subjects with AEs in the older age groups (>65 and >75 years). Overall, there does
               not appear to be major differences in the incidence of AEs by subgroup beyond what was
               observed in the general trial population. Some of the differences in AEs between the two
               treatment arms may be due to low enrollment within that subgroup. For example, there were only

               TEAEs occurred with similar frequency in both treatment arms – 31.9% of subjects in the
               ceftobiprole arm and 29.5% of subjects in the comparator cephalosporin arm (Table 88). The
               most common TEAEs in the ceftobiprole arm were vomiting (7.4% of subjects), viral infection
               (4.3%), headache (3.2%), pneumonia (3.2%), and alanine aminotransferase increased (3.2%), all
               with a risk difference of >3.0 compared to the comparator arm while the most common AE in the
               comparator cephalosporin arm was diarrhea (9.1% of subjects, risk difference -7.0). The
               ceftobiprole arm had more AEs related to hypersensitivity, phlebitis, urticaria, and infusion site
               reactions (6 subjects compared to 1 in comparator cephalosporin arm). The ceftobiprole arm also
               had more AEs related to the lower respiratory tract including pleurisy, pleural effusion and
               pneumonia (3 subjects compared to 0 in comparator cephalosporin arm) which are likely
               reflective of the infection under study and the 2:1 enrollment in the ceftobiprole versus
               comparator arms.
               There were only 5 subjects in the ceftobiprole arm with HABP included in the trial. Among these
               subjects, there were two AEs, chromaturia and pyrexia, neither of which were considered SAEs.

                        7.6.5. Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and
                              Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia, Trial
                              BAP 248/307
               The BAP 248/307 Trial was submitted to augment the safety database of ceftobiprole. The
               Applicant is not seeking an indication for HABP/VABP. This trial will be briefly described
               below followed by a discussion of safety results.
               BAP 248/307 was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-control, prospective, multicenter
               trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of ceftobiprole compared to linezolid/ceftazidime in adult
               subjects diagnosed with HABP and VABP. Pertinent inclusion criteria included subjects
               clinically diagnosed with pneumonia after a minimum of 72 hours of hospitalization or residence
               in a chronic care facility and who had clinical signs/symptoms of pneumonia. Subjects who were
               pregnant or lactating, had renal impairment, hepatic dysfunction, who were HIV positive, or had
               a known or suspected condition that may have jeopardized adherence to protocol requirements
               were excluded from the trial. A total of 781 subjects were randomly assigned to the two study
               arms with a total of 772 subjects included in the safety analysis, 386 subjects in each arm. There
               were 567 subjects in the non-VABP subgroup (283 in the ceftobiprole arm and 284 in the
               linezolid/ceftazidime arm) and 205 subjects in the VABP subgroup (103 in the ceftobiprole arm
               and 102 in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm).

                         7.6.5.1. Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
                                 Summary, Trial BAP 248/307

                            7.6.5.5. Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events, Trial BAP
                                    248/307
               TEAEs occurred in a similar proportion of subjects in the two treatment arms at 77.5% for
               ceftobiprole and 77.7% for linezolid/ceftazidime (Table 100). The TEAEs that had the highest
               incidence in the ceftobiprole arm were bacterial infection, diarrhea, respiratory failure, pyrexia,
               hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and vomiting. Of these TEAEs, vomiting, bacterial infection,
               pyrexia, and hyponatremia had a >2% risk difference in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the
               linezolid/ceftazidime arm. There was also an imbalance in renal impairment and cardiac failure
               in the ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. The high incidence of overall
               TEAEs is likely due to the significant comorbidities of the subjects and their complicated disease
               course. A significant portion of subjects in this trial required intensive care management with
               extensive medical histories contributing to their illness. Of the TEAEs with an imbalance,
               bacterial infection and cardiac failure were likely related to underlying medical conditions.
               Hyponatremia was also noted in the laboratory findings (see section below). Vomiting was noted
               in the other clinical studies as associated with ceftobiprole. Renal impairment was not observed
               when examining the laboratory data (see Laboratory Findings section below). Please refer to

                            7.6.5.6. Laboratory Findings, Trial BAP 248/307
               The tables below summarize the laboratory data from Trial 248/307 (Table 101,Table 102,Table
               103,Table 104,and Table 105). In the ceftobiprole treatment arm, there were more cases of
               hyponatremia (19.4%) compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime treatment arm (14%). It appears
               this difference in cases of hyponatremia was largely driven by mild cases (between 130 and 132
               mEq/L). The remainder of the chemistry values were relatively balanced between the two
               treatment arms. Of note, hyponatremia will be listed as an adverse reaction in section 6 of
               labeling. Evidence of renal dysfunction in each arm was also overall balanced with elevated
               creatinine occurring in 8.4% of subjects in the ceftobiprole arm vs. 7.5% in the
               linezolid/ceftazidime arms. While in the ceftobiprole arm there were more cases of elevated
               alkaline phosphatase at 24.1% compared to linezolid/ceftazidime at 15.5%, elevations in AST,
               ALT, and bilirubin levels were overall balanced between the two arms and did not exceed more
               than 10% of all subjects. Elevations in cholesterol levels were also balanced between the two
               arms, however there were more cases of hypertriglyceridemia in the ceftobiprole arm (52.2%)
               compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm (43.3%). Outliers in hematology values were also
               overall balanced between the two arms, but lymphopenia occurred more in the ceftobiprole arm
               (33.1%) than linezolid/ceftazidime (27.7%).
               Overall, there does not appear to be major differences in the laboratory values between the
               treatment arms. The subject population in the Trial was fairly ill with multiple medical
               comorbidities that may be contributing to certain laboratory value outliers.

                    which showed ALT, AST, and bilirubin down-trending while alkaline phosphatase and GGT
                    were shown to be increased. No further blood work was performed. Upon enrollment, subject
                    had also received multiple other antibacterial drugs including piperacillin-tazobactam and
                    gentamicin for 1 day. Concurrent administration of these drugs may have contributed to an

                         7.7.1. Higher Mortality for Ceftobiprole Patients With
                               VABP in Trial BAP 248/307
               Issue
               Increased deaths were observed in the VABP subgroup of Trial BAP 248/307 in subjects in the
               ceftobiprole arm compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm.



                                                                                                                                              215


Reference ID: 5357793

               NDA 218275
               Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection)
               Background
               In Trial BAP 248/307, a subgroup analysis was done on the safety population based on their
               pneumonia diagnosis. Of the total 772 subjects, there were 205 VABP subjects with 103 subjects
               in the ceftobiprole arm and 102 in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm. It was noted that VABP
               subjects in the ceftobiprole arm had a higher rate of death compared to the subjects in the
               linezolid/ceftazidime arm. Although the trial was not submitted for an evaluation of efficacy, the
               increased deaths may have represented a safety issue in this subgroup of subjects. An in-depth
               analysis of the data was conducted to evaluate potential causes and reasons for the increased
               deaths in the VABP subgroup.

               Assessment
               The total deaths in Trial BAP 248/307 were overall balanced between both arms (23%
               ceftobiprole vs. 22% linezolid/ceftazidime). In the HABP (non-VABP) subgroup however, there
               were fewer deaths in the ceftobiprole arm at 18.7% compared to 21.1% in the
               linezolid/ceftazidime arm. This is contrasted by more deaths in the VABP subgroup among
               ceftobiprole subjects (33%) compared to the linezolid/ceftazidime arm (23.5%). Given this
               higher rate of death, the narratives for all the deaths in the BAP 248/307 trial were reviewed to
               determine whether the study drug was related to death. The study drug and death were
               considered unrelated by the FDA reviewer if the death occurred within 48 hours of receiving the
               first dose of treatment, the death occurred after receiving the last dose of treatment, or another
               cause of death was established in the narrative. If a subject who was diagnosed with VABP,
               initiated treatment, and subsequently expired within a day, the study drug likely would have not
               made a difference in the subject’s trajectory and the death was deemed unrelated to the
               treatment. In addition, if a subject completed treatment of study drug with resolution of their
               illness but expired afterwards, this was also considered unrelated as clinical cure was
               documented and the death was not considered treatment failure. Study drug and death were
               considered related if there was treatment failure characterized by worsening of VABP that led to
               death after 48 hours of initiating treatment or if the subject’s death was due to an AE related to
               the study treatment. There was one death related to an allergic reaction, presumably from the
               trial treatment in the HABP subgroup in a subject receiving linezolid/ceftazidime.
               Based on the narrative reviews, the death and study drug relatedness were balanced between the
               two trial arms in the overall trial population with 12.6% of the deaths in the ceftobiprole arm and
               14.3% of the deaths in the linezolid/ceftazidime arm deemed related to the study drug (Table
               108). This balance in study drug relatedness is also seen within the subgroups. HABP subject
               deaths related to the trial treatment was seen in 17% of the ceftobiprole deaths and 16.7%
               linezolid/ceftazidime deaths. In the VABP subject subgroup, both treatment arms had 5.9% of
               the deaths deemed related to the Trial drug.

               Conclusion
               Despite the increased deaths in the VABP subgroup who received ceftobiprole compared to
               those who received linezolid/ceftazidime, most of the deaths do not appear to be related to the
               study treatment itself. The increased deaths in the VABP subgroup may have been due to chance,
               as there was a small number of subjects in the VABP subgroup relative to the entire trial. In
               addition, the acuity and severity of illness in this subgroup may have led to increased deaths
               overall, thereby confounding the association between deaths and trial treatment. However,
               information on increased mortality in VABP subjects treated with ceftobiprole will be included
               in the ceftobiprole labeling as a warning, emphasizing that ceftobiprole is not approved for the
               treatment of VABP.

                         7.7.2. Imbalance in Adverse Events Related to
                               Thrombosis in Trial BPR-CS-009
               Issue
               An increased frequency of thrombosis was observed in the ceftobiprole arm as compared to
               daptomycin arm in the BPR-CS-009 trial. This was evaluated further as a key safety issue due to
               nonclinical signals of thromboembolic events discussed in Section 7.1 and summarized below.

               Background
               In the nonclinical/toxicology studies, there were findings of thrombi observed across species (at
               the injection site in the rat, marmoset, and dog) and emboli noted in marmosets in the heart, lung,
               kidney, mostly with administration of ceftobiprole for a duration of over 1 month. The Applicant
               stated that in the 13-week studies in rats and marmosets, the thrombus formation was around the
               tip of the infusion catheter. When examining the histological changes, it was consistent with
               mechanical irritation by the infusion catheter, subsequently causing vascular-wall irritation and
               subsequent thrombus formation. The mechanical irritation was attributed to the small size of the
               veins relative to the large size of the implanted catheter. Ultimately, it was thought that the
               thrombus formation was caused by local irritation and injury along with the higher
               concentrations of ceftobiprole as compared with the clinical studies.

               Assessment
               When grouping the PTs using the narrow FMQ, there was a slightly higher incidence of
               thrombosis in the ceftobiprole vs. the comparator arm.

                        8.1.5. Hepatic Impairment
               The effects of hepatic impairment on the PK of ceftobiprole have not been evaluated.
               Ceftobiprole does not undergo significant hepatic metabolism and has low plasma protein
               binding. As such, hepatic impairment is not expected to alter the elimination of ceftobiprole.
               Dosage adjustments are not necessary in patients with impaired hepatic function.

                        8.1.6. Body Weight
               A single-dose study was conducted to investigate the PK of ceftobiprole in subjects with morbid
               obesity in comparison to non-obese subjects. Exposure to ceftobiprole was lower in morbidly
               obese subjects attributed to a larger volume of distribution and a higher CL, resulting in ~17%
               lower exposure which is unlikely to be clinically relevant. No doses adjustment based on body
               weight were made in the phase 3 studies.
               The effect of weight was also evaluated in the adult population PK (PopPK) analysis and in the
               PK/PD target attainment analysis. Although body weight was a statistically significant predictor
               of interindividual variability in CL, central and peripheral volumes of distribution in the PopPK
               analysis, ceftobiprole dose adjustments based on body weight are not required to ensure
               sufficient PK/PD target attainment.

                        8.1.7. Gender
               The effects of gender on ceftobiprole PK were evaluated in two phase 1 studies, as a primary
               objective of study BAP00036 and a secondary objective of Study CSI-1004. Systemic exposure
               to ceftobiprole was higher in females, with 21% higher Cmax and 15% higher AUClast in
               BAP00036 and 24% higher Cmax and 14% higher AUC0-inf in CSI-1004, compared to males.
               The higher systemic exposure in females observed in these studies was attributed to a lower body
               weight in females.
               The effect of gender was also evaluated in the PopPK analysis. In the adult PopPK model,
               gender identified as statistically significant predictor of the interindividual variability observed in
               the peripheral volume of distribution but was not found to be clinically relevant. Dose
               adjustment is not indicated based on gender.

                        8.1.8. Other Intrinsic Factors
               The effects of adult age and race were evaluated in the PopPK analysis and were not identified as
               statistically significant covariates. Accordingly, dose adjustments based on age or race are not
               indicated.

                    8.2. Extrinsic Factors

                        8.2.1. Pharmacokinetics Based Drug-Drug Interactions
               Ceftobiprole as a Victim of Drug-Drug Interactions
               In hepatocytes, ceftobiprole was slowly metabolized to the open-ring hydrolysis product
               BAL1029 and does not appear to undergo significant hepatic metabolism.
               In vitro studies showed that ceftobiprole is not a substrate of P-glycoprotein (P-gp), breast cancer
               resistance protein (BCRP), multidrug resistance protein 2 (MRP2), bile salt export pump, organic
               anion-transporting polypeptide (OATP) 1B1, OATP1B3, or OCT1 in vitro. Ceftobiprole was a
               substrate of the renal uptake transporters organic anion transporter 1 (OAT1) and organic cation
               transporter 2 (OCT2) but not OAT3 in vitro. Ceftobiprole was not evaluated as a substrate of
               multidrug and toxin extrusion protein 1 (MATE1), or MATE2-K as active secretion does not
               contribute to ceftobiprole elimination.

               Ceftobiprole as a Perpetrator of Drug-Drug Interactions
               In vitro studies showed that ceftobiprole did not inhibit or induce cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A2,
               2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, or 3A4/5 at therapeutic plasma concentrations. Hence, ceftobiprole
               is unlikely to result in clinically relevant CYP-mediated DDIs.
               In vitro studies showed ceftobiprole was an inhibitor of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 but was not an
               inhibitor of P-gp, BCRP, OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, or OCT2.
               The in vitro transporter inhibition assessment based on calculated R values is outlined in Table
               118. A drug has the potential to inhibit a transporter in vivo if the R value is >1.1. Since the in
               vitro studies indicate that a drug is an OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 inhibitor, we recommend the
               Applicant conduct an in vivo drug interaction study evaluating ceftobiprole as an inhibitor of
               OATP1B1 and OATB1B3 transporters as a post-marketing requirement (see Section 14.1.5).

                        Reproductive Potential
               Nonclinical Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology and Lactation Data
               Intravenous administration of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium to pregnant rats and monkeys
               during organogenesis showed no evidence of adverse fetal developmental outcomes at doses
               approximately 1.4 times and 0.9 times the MRHD, respectively, based on BSA comparison.
               Intravenous administration of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium to rats 2-weeks prior to mating,
               during organogenesis, and through lactation resulted in no significant adverse fertility or fetal
               development effects in offspring at doses approximately 1.4 times the MRHD, based on BSA
               comparison. Slight reductions in number of pups born per litter and decreased postnatal survival
               up to day 4 after birth were associated with maternal toxicity (mortality, reduced food
               consumption and body weight gain in surviving females during gestation). No offspring adverse
               effects were observed in surviving pups during the postnatal postweaning development period
               (Days 5 through 22) at doses up to 360 mg/kg.
               Pregnant rats were administered ceftobiprole at doses of 175, 250, and 360 mg/kg/day from 14-
               days pre-mating through lactation/postpartum day 21. Ceftobiprole was excreted in rat milk at
               levels of approximately 20% of the corresponding maternal plasma ceftobiprole levels. The
               concentration of ceftobiprole in animal milk does not necessarily predict the concentration of
               drug in human milk.

               Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Pharmacokinetics
               The absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of ceftobiprole medocaril (BAL5788)
               and ceftobiprole (active metabolite, BAL9141) was investigated in multiple species.
               Pharmacokinetics were assessed in the mouse, rat, rabbit, cynomolgus monkey, marmoset and
               dog. Excretion was primarily investigated in the rat.

               Absorption
               Nearly all studies have been conducted via the intravenous route, except for juvenile toxicology
               study conducted in rats by the subcutaneous route.

               Distribution
               Low-to-moderate plasma protein binding (18 to 40%) was detected in mouse, rabbit, dog,
               monkey, and human plasma, across a concentration range of 30-300µM. A comparative study of
               mouse and human showed that protein binding in both species is low.
               In a rat exploratory quantitative whole body autoradiography study following a single
               intravenous administration of 14C radiolabeled ceftobiprole medocaril sodium (20 mg/kg),
               quantifiable levels of radioactivity (>0.29 mcg-equiv/g) were detected in all tissues with a low
               overall distribution into most organs and tissues. The highest concentrations of radioactivity 15
               minutes post-dose were found in the kidney (34.2 and 32.3 mcg-equiv/g in the cortex and
               medulla, respectively), skin (19.63 mcg-equiv/g), tooth pulp (19.17), liver (18.96 mcg-equiv/g),
               lung (17.3 mcg-equiv/g), blood (17.04 mcg-equiv/g), connective tissue (15.73 mcg-equiv/g),
               aorta (11.61 mcg-equiv/g) and stomach mucosa (11.98 mcg-equiv/g). Lower levels (below
               10 mcg-equiv/g) were detected in mandibular and mesenteric lymph nodes, adrenal gland,
               thyroid, adrenal gland, pituitary gland, salivary glands, lacrimal gland, harderian gland, pineal
               body and muscle with lowest levels detected in the brain and spinal cord (0.38 and 0.58 mcg-
               equiv/g, respectively). Elimination of radioactivity was rapid (declining over 10-fold in 7 hours)
               except for the kidney with an estimated half-life of over 24 hours. Elimination of radioactivity
               was predominantly by the renal route (82% of the dose within 48 hours). In a similar distribution
               study in mice, the highest concentrations of radioactivity across tissues were found in the
               coagulating gland (78.29 mcg-equiv./g), the excretory organs kidney (30.43 and 24.24 mcg-
               equiv./g in cortex and medulla, respectively) and liver (26.26 mcg-equiv./g), as well as in skin
               and aorta. Elimination from tissues was rapid (declining concentrations by 10fold in 2 hours)
               with detectable levels only in the kidney cortex and liver by 24 hours.

               The parent pro-drug compound BAL5788 is rapidly metabolized to BAL9141. BAL941 is

                    animals (2 hours). These finding correlated with a dose dependent increase in plasma levels

               Local Tolerance

               TOX7588. A Local Irritation Study of BAL5788 by Intravenous Injection to Rabbits

               Methods
               The purpose of this study was to test the irritation potential of 2 ceftobiprole medocaril sodium
               formulations made from slightly different synthesis routes (BAL5788 A, intended for dilution in
               saline and B intended for dilution in 5% dextrose). BAL5788-A (drug product [DP] formula,
               batch # 30-4EXP, 91.6% purity); BAL-5788-B (New DP formula, batch # I050605, 100.9%
               purity) in 5 % dextrose was administered by IV injection to male Kbt rabbits (2.9-3.4 kg, 15
               weeks old, 3/group) into the ear vein (0.05 mL/site/day) once daily for 8 consecutive days.
               Positive control bromosulfalein (BSP) diluted into saline. Clinical signs (daily), body weight
               (prior to administration), observations of the injection site, and histopathology of the injection
               site (Day 8) were conducted/observed.

               Results
               There were no clinical signs. Body weights did not change significantly from controls. At
               10 mg/mL very slight to slight inflammation was observed in most rabbits (including controls)
               around the injection site between Days 3 and 5. Positive control rabbits showed slight or
               moderate inflammation along with thrombi throughout the dosing period. With the exception of
               the positive control animals where cell infiltration, desquamation edema, fibrosis, hemorrhage
               and thrombus were noted, there were no noteworthy findings. There were no significant
               differences in local irritation between the BAL5788 formulations A and B; BAL5788 was no
               more irritating than normal saline this 8- day study in rabbits.

               TOX7904. A Local Irritation Study of BAL5788 by Intravenous Injection to Rabbits-2

               Methods
               BAL-5788-B (formula, batch # I050605, 100.9% purity), vehicle (5% dextrose) or positive
               control BSP were administered intravenously into the ear vein at 0, 2 and 10 mg/mL either as
               fresh solution or aged for 30-hour period to male Kbt:JW rabbits (2.9-3.3 kg, 16 weeks old,
               3/group) for 8 consecutive days.
               Clinical signs (daily), body weight (prior to administration), observations of the injection site,
               and histopathology of the injection site (Day 8) were conducted/observed.

               Results
               There were no abnormal clinical signs or changes in body weight. There were no dose dependent
               changes in inflammation as compared to physiological saline at the injection site. The BSP
               animals showed slight to moderate inflammation and small thrombi. No significant differences in
               microscopic observations were made with BAL5788 or physiological saline. The positive
               controls showed cell infiltration, desquamation edema, fibrosis, hemorrhage and thrombi. Aging
               BAL5788 did not result in greater local irritation potential.

               TOX 7589. An Antigenicity Study of BAL5788 in Guinea Pigs

               Methods
               For passive sensitization, male Hartley guinea pigs were injected subcutaneously (6 sites on the
               dorsal skin of 2 animals) with serum from the actively sensitized animals, then 4 hours later
               challenged with 25, 50 or 100 mg/kg of intravenously administered BAL5788 and Evan’s blue
               dye. The dorsal skin was then examined for dye leakage. Actively sensitized animals were
               challenged with 100 mg/kg BAL5788 (pro-drug) and the reactions observed. Intravenous
               sensitization was evaluated at 1) 10 mg/kg/ BAL5788 (5 times week for 3 weeks, 2) 50 mg/kg/
               BAL 5788 (5 times a week for 1 week) and 20 mg/kg (5 times week for 2 weeks, 3) 10 or
               50 mg/kg, emulsified with Freund’s complete adjuvant (FCA) or Freund’s incomplete adjuvant
               (FIA) once weekly for 3 weeks. Positive control was 1 mg/kg subcutaneous ovalbumin
               emulsified with FCA once weekly for 3 weeks. The negative control was 5% dextrose IV or
               subcutaneous with FCA or FIA once weekly for 3 weeks. A 100 mg/kg challenge dose of
               BAL5788 (batch 30-4EXP, 93.8% purity) was used.

               Results
               One animal in the 50 mg/kg intravenous sensitization group died at day 4. No significant changes
               were noted in body weight. No abnormalities were seen in the sensitization with 5% dextrose or
               10 mg/kg BAL with or without FCA/FIA. In the 50/20 mg/kg BAL alone groups, scratching and
               piloerection were observed in 1/5 guinea pigs (ASA grade 1). In the 50 mg/kg group with
               FCA/FIA, anxiety, tremor, piloerection, dyskinesia, dyspnea were seen in all animals within 60
               minutes of challenge and 1/5 animals died (ASA reaction scores were 1/5 at 1, 2/5 at 2, 1/5 at 3
               and 4). In the positive control group, one animal died within 6 minutes of challenge (ASA 4)
               while the remaining 4 animals had an ASA reaction grade of 2. No reactions were noted in the
               BAL5788 passively challenged animals. The positive control had 5/5 animals positive. BAL5788
               was shown to have moderate antigenic potential.

               Report 10016. Ro 63-9141/001: Phototoxicity Study (In Vitro)

               Methods
               The potential phototoxic potential of Ro 63-9141/001 (ceftobiprole, batch # 18116B2, 370-
               4500 mcg/mL) was evaluated an in vitro assay with Balb/c 3T3 mouse fibroblasts by incubating
               the test article in the cell culture system with or without exposure to a non-cytotoxic dose of
               ultraviolet light (ultraviolet A [UVA] wavelength of 240-4500 nanometers) or kept in the dark.
               Cytotoxicity was expressed as a dose dependent reduction of the growth rate of cells as
               determined by uptake of the vital dye Neutral Red one day after treatment. Negative control was
               the vehicle, PBS/ 3% dimethyl sulfoxide [DMSO]) and chlorpromazine was used as positive
               control.

               Report 1004008. Ro 65-5788/001: In Vitro Assessment of Hemolysis, Plasma Turbidity and
               Plasma Precipitation in Dog Blood
               Methods
               The potential of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium (13.3% or 133.3 mg/mL pro-drug,
               batch# 90402B2171202) to induce hemolysis and plasma turbidity was evaluated in vitro using
               venous dog blood. Vehicles used were saline and 5% glucose. Hemolysis was measured by
               spectrophotometer (hemoglobin %) and turbidity was evaluated visually.

               Results
               No significant hemolysis or plasma turbidity or precipitation were seen in dog blood under in
               vitro conditions in a 13.33% test solution of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium pro-drug
               (corresponding to 10% or 100 mg/ml of the active drug Ro 63-9141/000) at concentrations
               corresponding to 1.25% (12.5 mg/ml pro-drug). At higher concentrations, hemolysis of up to
               7.3% and moderate to marked plasma turbidity and precipitation were observed.

               Tox7587. Haemocompatibility Test with Human, Rat, and Marmoset Blood

               Methods
               Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium was evaluated at 5 concentration levels (1, 5, 12.5, 25 and
               50 mg/mL) for hemocompatibility with rat, marmoset, and human blood at a volume ratio of 0.2,
               0.4 and 0.8 (1:5, 2:5 and 4:5) test material:blood. Reportedly, in the human, this ratio
               corresponds to administration of 1.6, 3.2 and 6.4 mL/min intravenous infusion rates. Hemoglobin
               release was determined following a 3-minute incubation at 37°C. For the plasma compatibility
               evaluation rat, marmoset, and human plasma were mixed with ceftobiprole medocaril sodium
               solutions at a ratio of 0.8 (4:5) test material:plasma. Samples were observed for flocculation,
               precipitation, and coagulation after 0.16, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 30 and 60 minutes at room
               temperature.

               Results
               No test article related hemolysis was observed at any dose tested in rat, marmoset. or human
               blood. When ceftobiprole medocaril sodium was mixed with human, rat, or marmoset plasma at
               a ratio of 0.8 (equivalent to an infusion rate of 6.4 mL/minute), dose dependent adverse reactions
               were observed (flocculation, precipitation, and coagulation) with increasing ceftobiprole
               medocaril sodium concentrations and increasing time. In all three species the adverse reactions
               (primarily precipitation) were observed ≥2.5 mg/mL concentration level. At ≥25 and with
               increasing time periods, flocculation and coagulation were also observed.

                                13.1.2.5.3. Safety of Impurities
               Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection (pro-drug (BAL5788) for ceftobiprole, BAL9141)
               will be given as an intravenous infusion and will be marketed as a sterile lyophilized powder for
               reconstitution (inactive ingredients are citric acid monohydrate in sodium hydroxide). There are
               no pharmacology/toxicology concerns for the excipients. The unit dose is 667 mg of ceftobiprole
               medocaril sodium per vial (equivalent to 500 mg of ceftobiprole). The MRHD is 2.67 g/day
               (equivalent to 2.0 g ceftobiprole). The animal data supports safety of ceftobiprole medocaril
               sodium for up to 1 month duration, however, based on clinical data treatments for up to six
               weeks were permitted. We deferred to the clinical review team on the safety of ceftobiprole
               medocaril sodium administered for this extended duration.
               The genotoxicity profile of ceftobiprole medocaril sodium was mixed including a negative Ames
               assay, a positive mouse lymphoma assay, a negative forward mutation assay, and positive
               chromosomal assays for both the pro-drug and active metabolite suggesting clastogenic potential.
               However, in vivo ceftobiprole medocaril sodium was negative in both the micronucleus assay
               and rat liver unscheduled DNA synthesis reducing concern for potential clastogenic activity.
               In considering potential and actual impurities in the drug substance (DS) and DP, the Applicant
               assessed genotoxic potential of several impurities using Derek quantitative structure-activity
               relationship (QSAR) analysis (a second tool was not expected since initial phase 3 clinical trials
               were conducted prior to the publication of the ICH M7 Guidance). Expert analysis based on
               available scientific literature or data from studies conducted by the Applicant and purging
               assessments were also considered. In general, the Applicant followed ICH M7, particularly in
               assigning a classification of mutagenic potential to the impurities. The Applicant considered 155

               purging calculations or direct analytical methods to demonstrate absence of 57 compounds.
